full_text:
The NFL schedule started to trickle out in the weeks after the draft before the league revealed the entire 2026 schedule on May 14. Sportsbooks released their Week 1 opening lines and totals for games spanning Sept. 9-14, which kicks off with the __Seattle Seahawks__ hosting the __Dallas Cowboys__ in a matchup of last year’s Super Bowl participants. I recently released my updated [Post-Draft Power Rankings](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-power-rankings-post-draft#/), and I’ve included my line projection for every Week 1 contest.

The battle of former first overall picks between Baker Mayfield and the __Tampa Bay Buccaneers__ and Joe Burrow and the __Cincinnati Bengals__ is the only game with a total in the 50s on the board at 51.5 points. The __New York Jets__ and __Tennessee Titans__ are on the other end of the spectrum with the lowest total at 38.5 points, and the __Cleveland Browns__ and __Jacksonville Jaguars__ total is also south of 40 points. The __Los Angeles Chargers__ are the biggest favorites on the board as 9.5-point home favorites over the __Arizona Cardinals__. Three games are tied for the tightest spread at 1.5 points. It’s time to dive into these matchups to see if there are any lines that we should bet on now or if there are any lines we should hold off betting until closer to the start of the season.

\>Be sure to check out [Brolley’s Best Bets: 2026 NFL Futures](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/series/2025/best-bets) for my favorite futures bets all offseason…Subscribe to the Best Bets Podcast on your [favorite platform](https://www.fantasypoints.com/media/podcasts/show/nfl-best-bets) and on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@FantasyPointsBetting) for year-round NFL betting talk…Join our “#official-bets” [Fantasy Points Discord](https://www.fantasypoints.com/media/discord) to see our staff's wagers as soon as we make them!

__Week 1 Opening Lines__
------------------------

\>Lines courtesy of [FanDuel Sportsbook](https://pa.sportsbook.fanduel.com/navigation/nfl?tab=games) as of May 14.

 Matchup Time New England Patriots at Seattle Seahawks (-4.5, 45.5) 9/9 8:20 p.m. San Francisco 49ers vs. Los Angeles Rams (-2.5, 49.5), Australia 9/10 8:35 p.m. Chicago Bears (-2.5, 45.5) at Carolina Panthers 9/13 1 p.m. Cleveland Browns at Jacksonville Jaguars (-7.5, 39.5) 9/13 1 p.m. Atlanta Falcons at Pittsburgh Steelers (-2.5, 41.5) 9/13 1 p.m. New York Jets at Tennessee Titans (-2.5, 38.5) 9/13 1 p.m. Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5, 51.5) 9/13 1 p.m. Baltimore Ravens (-3.5, 49.5) at Indianapolis Colts 9/13 1 p.m. New Orleans Saints at Detroit Lions (-7.5, 48.5) 9/13 1 p.m. Buffalo Bills (-1.5, 44.5) at Houston Texans 9/13 1 p.m. Miami Dolphins at Las Vegas Raiders (-3, 40.5) 9/13 4:05 p.m. Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Chargers (-9.5, 46.5) 9/13 4:05 p.m. Washington Commanders at Philadelphia Eagles (-4.5, 47.5) 9/13 4:25 p.m. Green Bay Packers (-1.5, 46.5) at Minnesota Vikings 9/13 4:25 p.m. Dallas Cowboys (-2.5, 46.5) at New York Giants 9/13 8:20 p.m. Denver Broncos at Kansas City Chiefs (-2.5, 43.5) 9/14 8:15 p.m. 

NFL Kickoff Game
----------------

#### __New England Patriots at Seattle Seahawks (-4.5, 45.5)__

\>Brolley’s [Power Ranking](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-power-rankings-post-draft#/) Projection: Seahawks -5

The NFL season kicks off with a rematch of the final game of the 2025 season. The Seahawks dominated the Patriots in a 29-13 victory as 4.5-point favorites to win the franchise’s second Lombardi Trophy. This matchup opened up in a similar spread range, even with the Seahawks receiving their Super Bowl rings in front of the “12s”. Seattle heads into the season with rookie __Jadarian Price__ taking over the backfield for Super Bowl MVP __Kenneth Walker__, who moved to the Chiefs in free agency. New England’s offseason has been filled with turmoil because of __Mike Vrabel__’s off-the-field transgressions.

Australia Game
--------------

#### __San Francisco 49ers vs. Los Angeles Rams (-2.5, 49.5)__

\>Brolley’s [Power Ranking](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-power-rankings-post-draft#/) Projection: Rams -2

The NFL heads to The Land Down Under for the first time. Aussies will get an entertaining introduction to tackle football with an important NFC West showdown. Los Angeles sits atop my Power Rankings after addressing its biggest need this offseason by adding Kansas City CBs __Trent McDuffie__ and __Jaylen Watson__. They’ll immediately be tested by San Francisco’s big offseason addition, __Mike Evans__, who left Tampa Bay for the first time to chase a second Super Bowl. The Rams and 49ers split two matchups outright and ATS last season, with both games finishing over the total. The winner will get a quick leg up in what should be an extremely competitive division — the top three NFC West teams combined for 38 wins last season. A win will also make the 15-hour flight back to California much more enjoyable.

Sunday
------

#### __Chicago Bears (-2.5, 45.5) at Carolina Panthers__

\>Brolley’s [Power Ranking](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-power-rankings-post-draft#/) Projection: Bears -1

The Bears, Panthers, and their quarterbacks will forever be connected because of a blockbuster trade between the franchises in March 2023. The Panthers selected __Bryce Young__ first overall in 2023 with a pick acquired from the Bears. The Bears then selected __Caleb Young__ first overall a year later with a pick they acquired from the Panthers after Carolina finished with the NFL’s worst record in Young’s rough rookie season. Both teams started to turn a corner last season by reaching the postseason. The Panthers ended a seven-year playoff drought, and the Bears terminated a four-year postseason dry spell.

#### __Cleveland Browns at Jacksonville Jaguars (-7.5, 39.5)__

\>Brolley’s [Power Ranking](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-power-rankings-post-draft#/) Projection: Jaguars -5.5

The Jaguars completed an audacious trade-up with the Browns last spring to select __Travis Hunter__ at No. 2, who will be back in the lineup for the first time since his knee injury in late October. The Browns turned their extra picks into __Quinshon Judkins__, __Dylan Sampson__, and __KC Concepcion__, who will be key pieces in __Todd Monken__’s new offense. The big question is, will it be __Deshaun Watson__ or __Shedeur Sanders__ getting those offensive weapons the ball in the season opener? The Jaguars were awfully quiet in free agency coming off their fifth division championship in franchise history, and they were universally panned for their haul in the draft. They can quickly silence the critics by taking care of business as the second-largest Week 1 favorite.

#### __Atlanta Falcons at Pittsburgh Steelers (-2.5, 41.5)__

\>Brolley’s [Power Ranking](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-power-rankings-post-draft#/) Projection: Steelers -3.5

The Falcons and Steelers will open the season with an inter-conference showdown for the second time in the last three years. Pittsburgh beat Atlanta 18-10 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in 2024 in a game that featured seven field goals and just one touchdown. The Steelers will see a familiar face on the opposite sideline as __Kevin Stefanski__ takes over in Atlanta after a six-year run in Cleveland. Pittsburgh is also starting a new era, with __Mike McCarthy__ taking over for __Mike Tomlin__ after a 19-year run without a losing record. __Tua Tagovailoa__ is likely to open the season as Atlanta’s quarterback, while Pittsburgh continues to await word from __Aaron Rodgers__ for the 2026 season.

#### __New York Jets at Tennessee Titans (-2.5, 38.5)__

\>Brolley’s [Power Ranking](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-power-rankings-post-draft#/) Projection: Titans -2.5

The Jets will face a prominent former employee to open the season for the second straight year. They dropped a 2-point decision against the __Aaron Rodgers__\-led Steelers last September, and they’ll travel to Nashville to take on their former coach, __Robert Saleh__, and the revamped Titans. Saleh will roll out several former Jets, including __Jermaine Johnson__, __John Franklin-Myers__, and __Solomon Thomas__. The Jets and Titans tied the Raiders and Cardinals for the NFL’s worst record last season, and a victory in the season opener will get one of these teams a third of the way to their win total from 2025. Points will be at a premium in this matchup, as this game features the lowest total on the board.

#### __Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5, 51.5)__

\>Brolley’s [Power Ranking](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-power-rankings-post-draft#/) Projection: Bengals -4

Cincinnati’s revamped defense will face an early test against a Buccaneers’ offense that’s going into its first season without __Mike Evans__ for the first time since 2013. The bookmakers don’t believe much has changed for the Bengals' defense, with this game featuring the highest total on the board at 52.5 points. Both teams are trying to return to prominent spots in their respective conferences, and a Week 1 victory could go a long way for one of these teams. The Bengals are looking to end a three-year postseason drought after advancing deep into the playoffs in 2021-22. The Buccaneers are trying to get back to the top of the NFC South after the Panthers ended their four-year run at the top of the division.

#### __Baltimore Ravens (-3.5, 49.5) at Indianapolis Colts__

\>Brolley’s [Power Ranking](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-power-rankings-post-draft#/) Projection: Ravens -3.5

The Ravens are entering unfamiliar territory as they embark on their first season without __John Harbaugh__ on the sidelines since 2007. Baltimore handed the reins to __Jesse Minter__, who is looking to return the Ravens to the top of the league after they failed to win double-digit games for just the second time in eight years with __Lamar Jackson__ on the roster. The Colts will open the season at home for the fourth straight season. They’re looking to start a Week 1 winning streak after ending an 11-game losing skid in season openers last year. The Colts started with an 8-2 record before losing seven straight contests, thanks in large part to __Daniel Jones__ playing through a hairline fibula fracture before tearing his Achilles early in Week 14. This line would rise to closer to a touchdown if Jones isn’t quite ready to play in the season opener.

#### __Buffalo Bills (-1.5, 44.5) at Houston Texans__

\>Brolley’s [Power Ranking](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-power-rankings-post-draft#/) Projection: Bills -1

The Bills and Texans both have aspirations of returning to the top of their divisions. Buffalo’s five-year run at the top of the AFC East came to an end at the hands of the Patriots, which eventually resulted in an early exit in the Divisional Round and the firing of __Sean McDermott__. Houston failed to win the AFC South for a third straight year despite winning 12 games. They also exited the playoffs after two postseason games, and those postseason performances created questions about __C.J. Stroud__’s viability as the franchise quarterback moving forward. The Texans scraped out a 23-19 victory as 4.5-point home underdogs with __Davis Mills__ at quarterback in late November.

#### __New Orleans Saints at Detroit Lions (-7.5, 48.5)__

\>Brolley’s [Power Ranking](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-power-rankings-post-draft#/) Projection: Lions -6

The Saints are an NFC team on the rise this offseason, and the Lions are moving in the opposite direction in the conference. Despite their converging paths, oddsmakers believe the Lions are still a class or two above the Saints entering the season based on the second-largest point spread on the slate. New Orleans surged late in the season under __Tyler Shough__, and the Saints' passing game will test a potentially shaky Detroit secondary, which hopes to have __Brian Branch__ (Achilles) and __Kerby Joseph__ (knee) available for the season opener.

#### __Miami Dolphins at Las Vegas Raiders (-3, 40.5)__

\>Brolley’s [Power Ranking](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-power-rankings-post-draft#/) Projection: Raiders -1

The Raiders landed the big prize in this year’s weak draft class, but __Fernando Mendoza__ could start his career watching from the sidelines if minority owner __Tom Brady__ has as much power as it seems from the outside. __Kirk Cousins__ would see the initial snaps in __Klint Kubiak__’s offense, and __Jeff Hafley__’s defense will look to frustrate the veteran quarterback. Miami will also debut a new quarterback in __Malik Willis__, but he’ll have little to work with at receiver among the likes of __Jalen Tolbert__, __Tutu Atwell__, and __Malik Washington__.

#### __Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Chargers (-9.5, 46.5)__

\>Brolley’s [Power Ranking](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-power-rankings-post-draft#/) Projection: Chargers -8

This interconference matchup has the least amount of juice on the slate, and it features the largest point spread of the opening week. Arizona will show off its newest toy, __Jeremiyah Love__, whom the Cardinals are hoping can be an immediate difference-maker since he’s making the most guaranteed money ($53.0 million) at the position. The Chargers will debut their new-look offense under __Mike McDaniel__, who brought his motion-heavy, wide-zone rushing attack to Hollywood after a four-year run in South Beach.

#### Washington Commanders at Philadelphia Eagles (-4.5, 47.5)

\>Brolley’s [Power Ranking](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-power-rankings-post-draft#/) Projection: Eagles -6

The __Jayden Daniels__\-led Commanders appeared ready to have yearly marquee matchups against the Eagles after the NFC East foes squared off in the conference title game during his rookie season. Unfortunately, the NFL backloaded its two matchups until the final three weeks of last season, which meant Daniels never faced off against the Eagles. The NFL remedied the situation by having the teams square off in the season opener. Washington wants to announce its back to being a yearly contender in the NFC East in Week 1, while Philadelphia would love to beat a division opponent at home for the second straight year — they defeated the Cowboys in the NFL Kickoff Game in 2025. The Eagles also want to get their offense back on track under new playcaller __Sean Mannion__, and likely without __A.J. Brown__ if he’s traded after June 1.

#### __Green Bay Packers (-1.5, 46.5) at Minnesota Vikings__

\>Brolley’s [Power Ranking](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-power-rankings-post-draft#/) Projection: Packers -.5

The Packers and Vikings will renew their rivalry in their season opener, and Minnesota will do it with its fourth different starting quarterback to open the year in as many years. The Vikings reached nine wins last season despite a miserable quarterback situation led by the overmatched __J.J. McCarthy__. They brought in __Kyler Murray__ on a cheap deal to try to remedy the situation after the Cardinals ran him out of town. Green Bay hasn’t had issues starting out the season on a good foot, but they’ve faded late in the last two seasons. __Micah Parsons__ and __Tucker Kraft__ are both up in the air for the start of the season following ACL, and this line could draft closer to a pick-em if one or both of them aren’t ready for Week 1. The Packers easily handled the Vikings 23-6 in Lambeau Field in their one meaningful contest last season.

Sunday Night
------------

#### __Dallas Cowboys (-2.5, 46.5) at New York Giants__

\>Brolley’s [Power Ranking](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-power-rankings-post-draft#/) Projection: Cowboys -.5

After 18 seasons in Baltimore, the __John Harbaugh__ era will begin in New York against an NFC East foe. The Cowboys and Giants will open the season against each other for the 13th time, with Dallas winning 11 of the first 12 matchups. Dallas slaughtered New York 40-0 at MetLife Stadium the last time these teams opened the season on Sunday Night Football in 2023. Dallas won a 40-37 overtime thriller over New York in its lone meaningful game last season — the Cowboys sat key players in their Week 18 matchup — but the Giants covered as 4.5-point underdogs. This line will move closer to a pick-em line if both teams are at full strength, but it could tick toward the Cowboys if __Malik Nabers__ is unable to play early in the season because of his slow ACL recovery.

Monday Night
------------

#### __Denver Broncos at Kansas City Chiefs (-2.5, 43.5)__

\>Brolley’s [Power Ranking](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-power-rankings-post-draft#/) Projection: Chiefs -.5

Does the NFL know something about __Patrick Mahomes__’ availability early in the season? I figured the schedule makers would backload Kansas City’s primetime games and division contests just in case Mahomes was unable to play in the first month of the season. Instead, the Chiefs have one of their most important games on Monday Night Football in the season opener at Arrowhead Stadium. The Broncos made a splashy move to acquire __Jaylen Waddle__, but they’ve otherwise flown under the radar after ending Kansas City’s nine-year run as the NFC West champions. __Bo Nix__ and the Broncos ended Kansas City’s slim hopes of continuing its division title streak with a game-winning, last-second field goal at Mile High in the middle of November, which was the only showdown between the Broncos and the Mahomes-led Chiefs last season. I lean toward taking the points with the Broncos in this early-season showdown against a potentially rusty Mahomes.

title: Finding the Next Jaxon Smith-Njigba: Playcaller Tendencies

full_text:
Before the 2025 season, Jaxon Smith-Njigba was a solid-but-not-elite player in the eyes of most. Relatedly, he’d run just 58 total career routes (5.2%) on plays with two or fewer WRs on the field.

After the 2025 season, Smith-Njigba is universally viewed as one of the NFL’s best receivers. This time, he ran a whopping 181 routes with two or fewer WRs on the field (37.8%) — roughly triple his previous career total — while leading the NFL in receiving yards on these plays (919).

Most notable was Smith-Njigba’s *efficiency* from these heavier personnel groupings. We’re talking about a clear minority of his routes — again, *__37.8%__*, to be exact — accounting for roughly half of all his production. *__51%__* of Smith-Njigba’s receiving yards and *__48%__* of all his fantasy points were scored on this specific subset of plays!

 Jaxon Smith-Njigba's fantasy points by year with... 3 or more WRs on the field 2025: 186.2 2024: 235.2 2 or fewer WRs on the field 2025: 174.7 2024: only 17.8 He ran 97 fewer total routes in 2025, but improved from the WR19 to the WR2 by FPG. (via @FantasyPtsData ) — Ryan Heath (@RyanJ_Heath) April 30, 2026 

And this isn’t only true of Smith-Njigba. __All WRs are more efficient when there are fewer WRs on the field for them to compete with, on average.__ Intuitively, an additional blocking TE or FB entering the game to replace a receiver means more targets for everyone else. The worst WR on an NFL roster is still an exponentially better target-earner than the best pass-catching fullback in today’s game (big ups to Larry Centers). The fewer WRs there are on the field (the more FBs and blocking specialist TE2s), the less the target competition, and the easier it is for the remaining WRs to earn targets and score fantasy points.

![](STATIC_ASSET_URI/photos/e970977c2b9047526417b79000752b35393f0c55/c2aa0a8a66eb452b0cba51ffe2c8325070df7fb7)

This efficiency hack is both broadly applicable to the NFL *and* shouldn’t have been difficult to use in predicting Smith-Njigba’s breakout, even pre-hindsight. Klint Kubiak — even then known as one of the masters of 2-WR sets — was replacing Ryan Grubb, who ran 11 personnel-based spread offenses at Washington and Seattle.

I [laid out the entire case in detail last summer](https://x.com/RyanJ_Heath/status/2008308356101140523?s=20), but foolishly glossed over it and failed to draft any Smith-Njigba. That was my biggest and most impactful mistake of the 2025 season; today, I’m going to rectify it.

2026 Fantasy Football Breakout Candidates: New NFL Playcaller Personnel Tendencies
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

__TL;DR:__ These are a sampling of the biggest player takeaways from this article, but there are several more! I’ve listed winners and losers for every offense discussed at the top of each team section for easy reference.

+ __Ladd McConkey__ ran only 9.9% of his routes from sets with fewer than 3 WRs in 2025. For comparison, that number was 46% for new Chargers OC Mike McDaniel’s Jaylen Waddle! McConkey is my favorite bet to be this year’s JSN.

+ __Drake London__ 3.13 YPRR on plays with 2 or fewer WRs ranked 9th-best in the NFL last year. His 0.61 FP/RR on these plays was nearly twice that of the Falcons’ next-closest receiver. He’s my favorite dark-horse candidate to lead the position in fantasy points.

+ __Christian Watson__ ran a route on 62.0% of the Packers’ dropbacks that featured 2 or fewer WRs last year, to Matthew Golden’s 43.3% and Jayden Reed’s 1.5%. Watson has always been a per-route superstar, and he finally looks locked into a full-time route share that should allow him to challenge for fringe-WR1 upside.

+ __Mike Evans__ averages a gargantuan 0.34 TPRR (would have ranked ~WR2 last year) and 2.97 YPRR (~WR3) with 2 or fewer WRs on the field since 2022, +36% and +31% more than he averages across all plays. If his health cooperates, he’s an amazing bounce-back candidate.

+ When the Bears had 3 TEs on the field in 2025, __Colston Loveland__ averaged an absurd 4.66 YPRR and a 53% receiving yards market share. I believe he’ll lead the Bears in receiving this year and cement himself into the position’s top tier alongside Brock Bowers and Trey McBride.

+ __Sam LaPorta’s__ 0.70 FP/RR from multi-TE sets over the past two seasons ranks 5th-best among WRs, behind only Puka Nacua, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Davante Adams, and Stefon Diggs. By early ADP, he’s one of the most mispriced players on all platforms to me.

Personnel Tendencies By Playcaller
----------------------------------

Below, I’ve calculated the percentage of each NFL playcaller’s *pass plays* for which they had 3 or more WRs vs. 2 or fewer WRs on the field. For the remainder of this article, I’ll be referring to these numbers as “dropback 3+ WR rate” and “dropback [1] For those curious, [this second chart](https://x.com/RyanJ_Heath/status/2054597793579249854?s=20) also displays the change in dropback [2] 

That only leaves the WR room as the potential beneficiaries of a condensed target tree. The player with the most to potentially gain compared to last year is unquestionably Ladd McConkey, who ran only 9.9% of his routes from sets with fewer than 3 WRs in 2025. For comparison, that number was 46% for McDaniel’s Jaylen Waddle!

As far as I can tell (as of early May), the Chargers haven’t given any indication that McConkey would be the WR to play in 1- and 2-receiver sets. (That small sample of work was relatively evenly split among the team’s non-Keenan Allen receivers last year, with Tre Harris actually taking a narrow 13-route lead over McConkey.) So there’s uncertainty here, but McConkey — as a WR who has flashed but hasn’t put together a full season of strong fantasy production entering Year 3 ([the most common breakout year](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2024/age-curves-when-nfl-players-break-out#/)), and could get to primarily compete with TEs and FBs for the first time — is one of the better analogues to Jaxon Smith-Njigba in this entire article.

Year 3 breakouts of Smith-Njigba’s magnitude don’t happen often, and it shouldn’t be our base expectation. But understand that to this point in their respective careers, McConkey has shown more alignment versatility (31% of his career routes have come on the outside to Smith-Njigba’s 22%) and downfield ability (68.5 to 53.3 air yards per game). McConkey also beats Smith-Njigba by most per-route and per-game stats, has accumulated nearly 200 more career receiving yards through two seasons, and only really loses out slightly when comparing total targets and receptions (with most of Smith-Njigba’s being of the low-aDOT variety). 78% of blind poll voters below chose McConkey’s Years 1-2 profile to Smith-Njigba’s!

 Which of these WRs (stats from Years 1-2) would you bet on in Year 3? Player A 0.22 TPRR 1.97 YPRR 13.2 FPG Player B 0.22 TPRR 1.71 YPRR 11.8 FPG Assume both were top-40 picks, are getting new OCs, and just lost some target competition. A had a better Y1, B a better Y2. — Ryan Heath (@RyanJ_Heath) May 4, 2026 

This argument *does* somewhat suffer if the Chargers re-sign Keenan Allen again, as that would indicate more personnel packages that include a slot receiver (i.e., 3-WR sets) and pull Allen’s 20.7% target share (compared to 2024 D.K. Metcalf’s 20.4%) back out of McConkey’s target-earning potential. Smith-Njigba was also a much better college prospect than McConkey analytically.

But those are the only counter-arguments I could come up with that hold any weight for me. And for now, they’re at least cancelled out by the offense’s ceiling, given what Justin Herbert [did with a healthy Joe Alt](https://x.com/SmolaDS/status/2016872752330764356?s=20). We also can’t forget that McDaniel had the Dolphins average the 3rd-most yards per play (6.4, behind only the 2024 Ravens and 2023 49ers) of any team over the past five years when he last had a decent offensive line.

### Atlanta Falcons (OC Tommy Rees)

##### __Winners:__ Drake London, Kyle Pitts

##### __Losers:__ Jahan Dotson, Olamide Zaccheaus, Zachariah Branch

The duo of new Falcons HC Kevin Stefanski and OC Tommy Rees (the actual playcaller) ranked 2nd-highest among 2026 playcallers by dropback Best YPRR with 2 or fewer WRs on the field in 2025 [min 50 routes] - Packers lost Doubs + Wicks, drafted no WRs, have Kraft + Musgrave, and leaned slightly heavier last year. Watson 🚀? - New Falcons coaches Kevin Stefanski/Tommy Rees threw from these sets 3rd-most. London 🚀? pic.twitter.com/sKyVGyj8MS — Fantasy Points Data (@FantasyPtsData) April 29, 2026 

Whenever he’s back to full health, Tucker Kraft would also be a clear winner of further route consolidation and multi-TE sets. HC Matt LaFleur [suggested](https://youtu.be/n_tx3A3mR7g?si=U4a5gb7wjIaD6qrH) it would now be easier to give players more opportunities after the departures of Doubs and Wicks, adding further that “you want guys who want the football.” To that end, Kraft himself [wants more targets](https://youtu.be/55r85lPjXs4?si=AQH5ofWDRQkP7hWJ) and believes he could “take a lot of pressure off everyone else” if the team would just “put the ball in \[his\] hands.” Kraft is a hyper-efficient freak who [holds three of the top-seven TE seasons](https://x.com/FantasyPtsData/status/2027013530055049633?s=20) by YPTOE since 2023 and was on a TE1 overall pace in his four fully healthy games before tearing his ACL.

 Tucker Kraft in 3 games he’s appeared on the injury report (Weeks 3, 4, and 6): - 11.7% target share (~TE29) - 42.7 receiving YPG (~TE13) - 9.6 FPG (~TE19) In 4 games he hasn't (Weeks 1, 2, 7, and 8): - 23.5% target share (~TE2) - 85.3 receiving YPG (~TE1) - 21.1 FPG (~TE1) — Ryan Heath (@RyanJ_Heath) October 27, 2025 

The Packers just handed Jayden Reed a three-year extension with $20 million guaranteed, but they’ve never shown any desire to utilize him in heavier sets; he has just nine career routes with fewer than three WRs on the field, and as mentioned above, 2025 Round 1 pick Matthew Golden saw significantly more action in those situations even last year. It would be even more incredible news for both Watson and Kraft if Golden (17% career TPRR) were to make those sets over Reed (23% career TPRR), as competing with a low-TPRR field stretcher archetype would be *vastly* better for everyone else’s target volume. I’m not certain which of Reed or Golden will make these sets more across the full season, but it’s definitely something to watch for when the preseason begins.

Winners And Losers From 3-WR Sets (High Dropback 3+ WR Rates)
-------------------------------------------------------------

### New Orleans Saints (HC Kellen Moore)

##### __Winners:__ Chris Olave, Jordyn Tyson

##### __Losers:__ N/A

Last year, Saints HC Kellen Moore ranked 6th-highest among 2026 playcallers in dropback 3+ WR rate (80%) despite Devaughn Vele being this team’s WR2 for a significant chunk of the season. Now that they’ve spent the 8th overall pick on Jordyn Tyson ([my model’s favorite](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/season/2026/ryan-heaths-rookie-wr-rankings#/) WR from this rookie class), they appear poised to run it back.

As I discussed in my [2025 Takeaways](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/heaths-nfl-draft-fantasy-takeaways#/), these 11 personnel-heavy offenses are often the ones that provide enough dropback volume to produce *multiple* fantasy-relevant WRs. Last year, five offenses (the Bengals, Rams, Lions, Cowboys, and post-Meyers trade Jaguars) had two WRs rank inside the top-24 by FPG. All of them except the Bengals ranked in the top half of the league by dropback 3+ WR rate, and all ranked top-14 in total 11 personnel snaps. When you have two very good WRs both running lots of routes, it tends to create two productive fantasy receivers!

To reiterate the discussion from my [post-Draft landing spots](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/heaths-nfl-draft-fantasy-takeaways#/) piece, Moore has the “lots of routes” part covered; he’s virtually always ranked top-5 in pace. And this isn’t totally theoretical: both Chris Olave (17.6) and Rashid Shaheed (13.4) ranked as top-24 WRs by XFP/G last year until Shaheed was traded.

So I think it’s somewhat likely that the Saints are the next high-flying, high-volume passing attack in the vein of the Cowboys and Bengals of recent years that give us multiple strong fantasy receivers. ### Pittsburgh Steelers (HC Mike McCarthy)

##### __Winners:__ Germie Bernard

##### __Losers:__ DK Metcalf

The last time we saw Mike McCarthy calling plays, his Cowboys played a ton of 11 personnel, ranking 3rd-highest among current playcallers in dropback 3+ WR rate (84%). This will be a dramatic change from what Arthur Smith did with the Steelers last year, and the team’s selection of rookie Germie Bernard in Round 2 and their trade for Michael Pittman reinforces that Aaron Rodgers will be dropping back with 3 WRs on the field much more often than last year.

The most immediate impact is that Bernard should have a chance to play a near-full-time role in the slot out of the gate, and McCarthy’s primary slot receiver [has finished top-10 in FPG](https://x.com/ScottBarrettDFB/status/2048140386502406353?s=20) in over half of his seasons as an NFL head coach. He’s one to keep an eye on, but Bernard was [more of a floor play](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/ryan-heaths-rookie-wr-rankings#/) as a prospect, and there are a lot of CeeDee Lamb and Randall Cobb seasons in that McCarthy slot receiver stat, so I’m not bought into the idea that he’ll matter outside of best ball.

This said, it’s much clearer to me that DK Metcalf is a massive loser in this personnel exchange and a fade who fails to strike fear into my heart even at his ~WR37 ADP. Metcalf averaged the 2nd-most targets per game from 2-or-fewer receiver sets of any WR last year (4.2), scoring 55% of his fantasy points on these plays. Yet, despite all the inherent advantages offered to a clear No. 1 receiver like Metcalf by heavier personnel, he finished with just 12.5 FPG (~WR22) and only three spike weeks of 17.0 or more (one fewer than Wan’Dale Robinson). Metcalf’s target share dropped from 25.6% (~WR15) to just 19.0% (~WR42) whenever a third receiver did come onto the field — just barely ahead of teammate Calvin Austin (18.5%).

Even if the pass rate increases (and it will, at least compared to the Arthur Smith days), we just saw what happened when Metcalf played on an 11-personnel-heavy team that ranked 7th-highest in total dropbacks: he averaged just 12.9 FPG (~WR30) on the 2024 Seahawks. There just isn't any meaningful upside here, and I fully expect Michael Pittman to eat Metcalf’s lunch as a target-earner. Just look at how the two compare with three or more receivers on the field since 2023, despite Pittman’s primary target competition in Josh Downs (0.24 TPRR on these plays) being a better per-route target earner than Jaxon Smith-Njigba over his first two seasons (0.22). I don’t at all understand why there’s such a significant gap between the pair in ADP.

### Arizona Cardinals (HC Mike LaFleur)

##### __Winners:__ Marvin Harrison Jr. (maybe/if you can cope hard enough)

##### __Losers:__ Michael Wilson

47% of the 2025 Cardinals’ pass plays featured 2 or more TEs on the field (4th-most by a mile). Though new HC Mike LaFleur worked closely with Sean McVay in LA and could certainly implement some 13-personnel looks of his own (discussed below), the Rams were *well below* the Cardinals at 28% even last year. The last time LaFleur himself called plays (with the Jets in 2022), his 2-TE dropback rate was down at 20%, with 79% of pass plays coming with 3+ WRs on the field (would rank 7th-most among 2026 playcallers’ most recent season).

Even though LaFleur has said he’s excited about Tipp Reiman from a Y TE standpoint (via [CoachSpeak Index](https://x.com/CoachspeakIndex)), the team also signed Kendrick Bourne, a meaningful upgrade from all of the Cardinals’ WR3 options in 2025. Any way you slice it, we should assume this team will play significantly more 3-receiver sets than they did in 2025, and that’s probably bad for both Trey McBride and Michael Wilson, considering the manner in which they accumulated production last year.

Wilson [ranked 7th](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2025/ryan-heaths-fantasy-football-takeaways#/) in targets per game with 2 or fewer WRs on the field. __When a 3rd WR came on, his FP/RR fell all the way from 0.47 (~WR14) to just 0.30 (~WR51).__ A lot of that is surely [the impact of playing with or without Marvin Harrison Jr.](https://x.com/SmolaDS/status/2052778054921933040?s=20) expressed in a different way, but it’s meaningful from either lens. Heavy personnel was a boon to Wilson *precisely because* it often meant he was competing for targets with Elijah Higgins and “Xavier Weaver” (who accumulated a total of 1 target on 68 such routes, below a 2% TPRR) rather than Marvin Harrison Jr. and Kendrick Bourne, and that’s over now!

I don’t expect as large an impact on McBride, as he can simply play in-line in 11 personnel and won’t come off the field any more often. Still, his target share over the past two seasons falls from 32.3% with 2 or fewer WRs on the field to 25.1% with 3 or more, while also making for a 30% difference in YPRR. This is ultimately less concerning to me than the fact that the Cardinals’ pass rate (1st in PROE, +7.3%) and McBride’s [garbage time production](https://x.com/RyanJ_Heath/status/2015904201524559894?s=20) are also spots for potential regression, but ADP basically agrees, as McBride is currently the TE2 behind Brock Bowers on platforms like *Underdog*.

The more interesting effect of fewer 2-TE sets might actually be on Marvin Harrison Jr. Since the team didn’t have a viable 3rd WR in 2025 and didn’t play as much true 11 personnel, McBride ended up as the de facto slot receiver, with Harrison pinned to the outside. LaFleur has used his TEs more conventionally, with players like Tyler Conklin spending much more time in-line while the actual wide receivers rotate through the slot.

He ran 61.9% of his routes there, the most of any full-time TE (only Gesicki, Likely, and Andrews were ahead of him) Highest slot rate by a Mike LaFleur TE each year since 2021: 29.6% 32.9% 29.8% 19.2% 48.1% @FantasyPtsData — Ryan Heath (@RyanJ_Heath) May 8, 2026 

In fact, that’s basically what LaFleur said in [this press conference](https://youtu.be/DCslxyhEe1I?si=cLUEkIdG06XrZhpD) when asked whether Harrison would play in the slot or at X: “What has been really neat about the systems that I've been in \[and\] the system that we'll run is \[that\] who is the slot, who is the X receiver, that they're all interchangeable.”

So from Harrison’s point of view, a shift to more 11 personnel means he’s still always competing for targets with McBride and Wilson, but that he’ll perhaps have more chances available to rotate into the slot compared to before. Still, if you’ve thought that Harrison could benefit from more diverse usage (as [several](https://x.com/jagibbs_23/status/1886559205093408828?s=20) [have](https://x.com/jagibbs_23/status/1886559464482103532?s=20) [argued](https://x.com/MattHarmon_BYB/status/1928501480048243199?s=20), especially after his rookie season), he’s a lot more likely to get it this year than last.

Winners And Losers From Multi-TE Sets
-------------------------------------

As TEs flew off the board on Day 2 of the NFL Draft (often to teams who already possessed an every-down TE!), something hit me:

 All the sharpest offensive minds in the league are ritualistically sacrificing this shitty draft class so that we can continue getting 3.00 YPRR from all their good players https://t.co/uTrgR6WyHF — Ryan Heath (@RyanJ_Heath) April 25, 2026 

Playcallers like Sean McVay exploited defenses’ tendencies to [match the offense’s personnel](https://x.com/gregolsen88/status/1984741411657298239?s=20) and put fewer good coverage defenders on the field when faced with multiple TEs. The Rams deployed 13 personnel (3 TEs) [the most of any team over the past five years to create unparalleled dropback efficiency](https://x.com/ScottBarrettDFB/status/2047850625866649953?s=20).

Even if defenses catch on to that trick (and they will), as Max Toscano argues [here](https://x.com/maxtoscano1/status/1914777155549999379?s=20) and [throughout](https://x.com/maxtoscano1/status/1914779736469069959?s=20) this [thread](https://x.com/maxtoscano1/status/1914763527317021149?s=20), putting players on the field who can force defenses to commit more bodies to the box while maintaining both run and pass threats — i.e., TEs who can both block and catch, or WRs who can play the “F” as an effective-enough blocker — is massively helpful in creating explosive and efficient passing offense in today’s game.

To me, the Draft and free agency decisions of the four teams we’ll discuss below reflect an understanding of this idea. Like the teams we discussed above, they’ll have fantasy football winners and losers stemming from the realities of how heavy personnel affects intra-offense target competition and per-route efficiency. But I wanted to separate out these offenses as being on the cutting edge of the meta, creating the potential for all boats to be lifted.

### Chicago Bears (HC Ben Johnson)

##### __Winners:__ Colston Loveland

##### __Losers:__ Sam Roush

The Bears selected Sam Roush — a hulking 267-pound TE for whom I’m seemingly on an island among analytics people in [believing he has some juice as a receiver](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/ryan-heaths-rookie-te-rankings#/) — in the early 3rd round. Going to this TE depth chart nukes any prayer Roush may have had for his own fantasy-relevance, but it could promise good things for the offense as a whole. Maybe he’s just a long-term Cole Kmet replacement, but his selection at worst signals that the Bears are woke to the benefits of multi-TE sets, and at best could give them a filthy Rams-esque 13 personnel set as soon as this season.

Using the same logic from throughout this piece, this would benefit whichever one of the Bears' WRs remains on the field for these plays. The same would go for whichever two remain on the field in 12 personnel. So I understand the desire to solve that mystery.

 The people are buzzing about 13 personnel (1 WR, 3 TEs) after the Bears selected Sam Roush. Route participation rates on these plays in 2025: Colston Loveland - 97.8% D.J. Moore - 46.0% Rome Odunze - 27.6% Luther Burden - 23.3% It was usually Moore on 1WR sets. Who is it now? pic.twitter.com/8HHgWXr7XZ — Fantasy Points Data (@FantasyPtsData) April 28, 2026 

But ultimately, preseason usage is going to change whatever conclusion one might come to now. It’s also going to be hard to find a reliable answer in 2025 data: D.J. Moore took the plurality of those snaps and is now off the team, while Luther Burden and Rome Odunze had few overlapping games in which both were healthy and trusted as full-time players. The team could also simply split these snaps up evenly once again, meaning there is no singular answer or winner between Burden and Odunze.

And regardless of all that, the most surefire winner of a Bears’ offense that leans harder into heavier personnel would be Colston Loveland. __When the Bears played 13 personnel last year, he averaged an absurd 4.66 YPRR and a 53% receiving yards market share.__

Put another way, the Bears fully leaned into heavy personnel at the end of 2025. Beginning in Week 15, they played over half their offensive snaps with 2+ TEs on the field during five of their final six games, after doing so only once over their first 13. The result was that Loveland averaged 9.3 targets per game, 2.59 YPRR, and 16.0 FPG over that stretch. Respectively, those would rank 2nd-best, 3rd-best, and 5th-best among all TE seasons since 2021, or as the WR6, WR6, and WR9 among wide receivers last year. And among *rookie TEs*, there’d be no comparison: Brock Bowers had the most productive fantasy season among that cohort since the merger (15.5 FPG).

 The Bears' 12 and 13 personnel snap rates by week vs. Colston Loveland's fantasy points and volume (XFP) Not perfectly one-to-one, but the consistent volume and upside games came at the end of the season, as did the Bears' decision to have 2+ TEs on the field for >50% of snaps pic.twitter.com/JakFO62kgj — Ryan Heath (@RyanJ_Heath) May 11, 2026 

For all these reasons, I believe strongly that Loveland should be the first Bears pass-catcher selected in most formats. He averaged 16.0 XFP/G from Week 15 on, with no other WR/TE exceeding 11.4 over that stretch! He even dunked on per-route darling Luther Burden in TPRR (0.31 to 0.26) and FP/RR (0.53 to 0.50) despite actually playing a full-time role (73.4% to 58.8% route participation)! Based on what we most recently saw, Loveland just requires the least projection and personnel-related changes to succeed.

### Los Angeles Rams (HC Sean McVay)

##### __Winners:__ Puka Nacua

##### __Losers:__ Max Klare’s and Terrance Ferguson’s dynasty managers

This one is much simpler on the surface because we’ve seen the Rams [lean into](https://x.com/ScottBarrettDFB/status/2047850625866649953?s=20) multi-TE sets already, and we’ve confirmed the fantasy results. In 1- and 2-WR sets, Puka Nacua averaged a [completely insane](https://x.com/RyanJ_Heath/status/2053935099385675805?s=20) 6.25 YPRR last year (the most of any WR in the *Fantasy Points Data* era). Consequently, he comfortably ranks as my overall WR1.

But I’m not as convinced that the Rams’ selection of Max Klare — an even [better receiving prospect](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/ryan-heaths-rookie-te-rankings#/) than Roush, even if his selection gestures at a similar team philosophy when added alongside Terrance Ferguson, Colby Parkinson, and Tyler Higbee — is a boon for Davante Adams. It definitely [was at first](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2025/five-stats-to-know-week-10) (pre ~Week 13) when Adams was decisively getting on the field over Nacua in 1-WR sets, but that trend reversed over the final eight games. Even if ignoring the games Adams missed, Nacua started playing more than him in heavier sets:

 Puka Nacua vs. Davante Adams in 1- and 2-WR sets, post-bye - Accounted for 36% of Nacua's fantasy points vs. 61% of Adams' - Puka passed Adams in these Weeks 14 and 15 (pre-Adams injury) and didn't give them up in the playoffs - Adams 8 TDs to Puka's 1 @FantasyPtsData pic.twitter.com/uGuSdHaO5A — Ryan Heath (@RyanJ_Heath) May 11, 2026 

Even worse is that Adams was far more *reliant* than Nacua on these plays for his fantasy output; 61% of his post-bye fantasy points came from 1- and 2-WR sets, as he scored a whopping 8 TDs from them. Some of that is just from the Rams playing differently in the red zone (i.e., force-feeding Adams the ball), but this does make for a terrifying setup. Adams’ production was propped up by high-volatility TD scores from personnel groupings in which he played less and less as the season went on: could you write a better script for a 33-year old WR to suddenly hit the age cliff?

I didn’t list Adams as a definitive “loser” above because he *was* quite efficient in heavier sets last year (3.54 YPRR, 5th-best), and the efficiency gains of the offense could plausibly propel him to another double-digit TD season. It mainly speaks to his volatility — which I’d say is well-reflected in his WR26 *Underdog* ADP after last year’s WR9 per-game finish — due to the possibility he’s pushed off the field even more by Nacua in these high-leverage spots.

### Detroit Lions (OC Drew Petzing)

##### __Winners:__ Sam LaPorta

##### __Losers:__ Isaac TeSlaa

47% of new Lions OC Drew Petzing’s pass plays last year featured multiple TEs on the field (3rd-most among this year’s playcallers). The message that resonated the most on this earlier in the year was Dan Campbell [downplaying the idea](https://www.youtube.com/live/CqTk9IUquWc?si=l6amge_agLt_U9o4) that Petzing’s philosophy would carry over to the Lions, saying “that's where \[Petzing’s\] roster has gone…that's not something that…I foresee us being…we're going to be versatile.”

But virtually every other sign has pointed to the Lions leaning more into multi-TE sets than they did last year (22% of pass plays, 14th-fewest). When asked, Petzing himself connected 12 and 13 personnel directly to Campbell’s “versatility” angle, saying “To the earlier point of trying to stay flexible and adaptable…we can line up in 12 and be in 11 sets, we can be in 11 and line up in 12 sets, you can get into 13 and move people around the formation and kind of get into some different looks…the more you can do that the harder it is for a defense to kinda lock in on who you are and what you’re trying to do.”

TEs coach Steve Oliver [said a day earlier](https://youtu.be/m-xn1h-r2tA?si=fssj-5KYJsbc6AQI) that the Lions could be like a “chameleon” and oscillate between 12, 13, and 11 personnel on a weekly basis, depending on the opponent. And after all these interviews, the team signed Tyler Conklin, making their TE room plenty deep enough to back up that talk.

From the totality of these statements, it’s clear that versatility was a major topic of discussion in the Lions’ offseason meetings this year, and it sounds like that’s how Petzing has sold Campbell on his offense. So while I still expect some 11 personnel looks with Isaac TeSlaa running clear-outs, I could see the Lions being Rams-esque this year, in the sense that while they may rank merely “above average” in heavy personnel usage over the full season, they could feature it heavily within individual games, supporting fantasy football spike weeks for whichever players most benefit from it.

I’ll say first that I think TeSlaa (0.10 career TPRR), Conklin (0.15 over the past two seasons), or Wright (0.13) being on the field is equally good for both Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. I also wouldn’t expect heavy personnel to eat into either’s route share significantly, given all of the references in the interviews linked above to building the offense around the best players. That pair benefits from whichever direction the Lions go.

But multi-TE sets could be *especially* beneficial to Sam LaPorta, by virtue of both his historical efficiency on these plays (__his 0.70 FP/RR on them over the past two seasons ranks 5th-best among WRs, behind only Puka Nacua, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Davante Adams, and Stefon Diggs__) and simply locking him into more playing time. LaPorta ranks just 10th among TEs in route participation rate since entering the league (72.1%), but he’s always scored as a top-2 fantasy TE in games he’s played a true full-time role.

These splits could have as much to do with LaPorta’s health as with his opportunities (though partial games at the low end [don’t skew them](https://x.com/RyanJ_Heath/status/2054214384126136421?s=20)), but it’s pretty inarguable that more routes are a good thing for him. ### Las Vegas Raiders (HC Klint Kubiak)

##### __Winners:__ Brock Bowers, Michael Mayer

##### __Losers:__ N/A

What the Raiders *didn’t do* in the Draft and free agency felt pretty instructive. The most significant pass-catcher they selected was Malik Benson in Round 6. They signed Jalen Nailor to a discounted version of the contract Rashid Shaheed got from the Seahawks. The most significant remaining names on the free agent market are Stefon Diggs (who posted just 65.4% route participation last year, as the Patriots apparently never felt comfortable playing him in a true full-time role) and Deebo Samuel (an injury risk whose most efficient days are behind him, having now averaged below 2.00 YPRR and a 7.0 aDOT for two consecutive seasons).

Even if the team signs one of those players in July, there’s a real chance that Michael Mayer is the second-most effective receiver on this team. Over the past two seasons, Mayer has run a route on at least 66% of the Raiders’ dropbacks in seven games; in them, he averages 9.9 FPG (~TE17) on 9.5 XFP/G (~TE13), and Tre Tucker has only out-targeted him in two of the seven. If the Raiders primarily operate out of 2-TE sets — and why wouldn’t they, considering that new HC Klint Kubiak ran them at a top-6 rate last year and that their top-three WRs are Tucker, Nailor, and Jack Bech — I’d expect Mayer to finish as at least a high-end TE2.

Maybe that doesn’t move the needle outside of best ball (where Mayer appears as an excellent and unique final-round pick to me with loads of contingent upside to boot). But it does slightly increase my interest in Brock Bowers, who has posted a 90% route participation rate in these sets over his career (would rank ~TE1) compared to 74.9% (~TE6) in 1-TE sets.

And beyond any in-the-weeds personnel discussions, Bowers just averaged 16.4 FPG (~WR10) excluding the three games he played through a PCL sprain, on the NFL’s lowest-scoring offense of the past two seasons. He’s lost all his target competition and gets clear upgrades at playcaller and along the offensive line; why is he being drafted in virtually the same spot as he was last offseason?

Teams With Remaining Uncertainty
--------------------------------

I don’t have a hard take yet on where these two teams will lean personnel-wise. But the direction they choose could have a major impact on which of their pass-catchers achieve fantasy relevance, so I wanted to game out some scenarios for us to keep in mind as training camps open and more reporting surfaces.

### Cleveland Browns (HC Todd Monken)

You’ll notice at the top of this article that new Browns HC Todd Monken led the NFL in dropback Harold Fannin vs. Jerry Jeudy from weeks 1-16 (pre-groin injury) Fannin Targets: 102 Yards: 701 TPRR: 0.26 YPRR: 1.77 Jeudy Targets: 91 Yards: 531 TPRR: 0.18 YPRR: 1.06 Monken on Fannin this offseason: "He's a little like Brock Bowers..." https://t.co/NycGrOBBle — Ryan Heath (@RyanJ_Heath) April 24, 2026 

Another out for Fannin is that Monken could simply say “screw it” and play him at Y regardless of the impact it has on the run game. After all, Fannin [didn’t have](https://x.com/RyanJ_Heath/status/2039702297391870081?s=20) noticeable run/pass snap splits last year, and there’s [no other obvious candidate](https://x.com/RyanJ_Heath/status/2047840917936132515?s=20) for the every-down Y role on the Browns’ roster; neither Jack Stoll nor Blake Whiteheart got on the field enough to limit the F TEs in front of them on their respective depth charts last year, and the team only added TE Joe Royer in Round 5.

Some of Fannin’s success also came from the Browns being a bad team that trailed often in obvious dropback scenarios, which makes it easier for flex-only TEs to see the field. The Browns will likely be bad again this year!

 Here's every 11.0+ FPG TE season over the past three years Sorted by the % of their fantasy points scored when trailing by 7 or more... ...with surprise/"breakout" seasons from flex-only TEs highlighted. via @FantasyPtsData pic.twitter.com/Db8aHww66L — Ryan Heath (@RyanJ_Heath) May 7, 2026 

Unfortunately, Fannin’s TE6 ADP on most platforms (ahead of LaPorta!) suggests drafters currently feel a lot more certainty than I do. It wouldn’t take much of a shift in usage to spell disaster for Fannin here; even over the second half of 2025, his 71.2% route share (~TE16) was just on the edge of where we typically see fantasy-relevant TEs. Given the choice between a TE who may not run a full-time route share on the Browns, or two who very likely will on the Packers and Lions, I’m opting for the latter two.

### Jacksonville Jaguars

The Jaguars ranked top-5 in 3+-WR dropback rate last year (80%) to pretty great success, with Trevor Lawrence [playing the best football of his career](https://x.com/ScottBarrettDFB/status/2054220302020661294?s=20). They return playcaller Liam Coen, who already had a long history of maximizing the production of his slot receivers even before he got Parker Washington to average 15.2 FPG across 10 games (including playoffs) after Travis Hunter’s injury.

 Jaguars HC Liam Coen's slot WRs: a history. 2021: Wan'Dale Robinson averaged 102.6 receiving YPG at Kentucky, nearly double his previous seasonal high. 2022: Cooper Kupp averaged 11.4 FPG from the slot alone (an effective 46% route share) 2024: Chris Godwin averaged 14.3 FPG… pic.twitter.com/88HEtrKiu9 — Fantasy Points Data (@FantasyPtsData) August 14, 2025 

I largely left teams for whom I expected little change in players and personnel relative to 2025 out of this article, so what are the Jaguars doing here?

The uncertainty here stems from the Jaguars selecting blocking-only TE Nate Boerkircher in Round 2, with GM James Gladstone [explaining the pick](https://youtu.be/_92QthdsZ0U?si=WLaVEl-_xqWnn6de) by saying that “the trend in the NFL was that heavier tight end…sets were going to be something that got prioritized.” They doubled down by selecting Tanner Koziol (one of [my favorite sleeper TEs](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/ryan-heaths-rookie-te-rankings#/), though he projects as much more of a receiver than a blocker in heavy sets) in Round 5.

So, are the Jaguars going to roll out 12 personnel with Brenton Strange and one of Boerkircher or Koziol on the field for a significant percentage of their dropbacks this year? If they did, Jakobi Meyers would be the clearest beneficiary, as he easily led this receiver group in route participation rate from 1- and 2-WR sets after joining the team in Week 10 (68.8%, to Brian Thomas Jr’s 56.3%, and Washington’s 53.6%).

But I’m not fully convinced this is going to happen. On May 9th (via [CoachSpeak Index](https://x.com/CoachspeakIndex)), Coen remarked that he believes “that there is gonna be an uptick…in the NFL next year in heavier personnel groupings. __I’m not sure we’re gonna over-rotate to a point where we want to get slower or less explosive…we still have some pretty damn good wideouts that I like to use.__”

Given that comment, unless we hear or observe otherwise as training camps start up, I think it’s still most likely that the Jaguars will remain primarily an 11-personnel team. But this uncertainty definitely widens the ranges of outcomes for players like Meyers (who would love heavy personnel and gets to claim a bit more upside to his name from the possibility), Washington (who would seem the most likely to come off the field in 12), and Hunter (who I [believe has a better chance of neutralizing](https://x.com/RyanJ_Heath/status/2054282262750072878?s=20) Washington’s fantasy relevance than he’s been given credit for, regardless of how the personnel rates shake out).
